title: Materials, Corrosion, Haber Process and Fertilisers

flashcard_questions.q: The gradual destruction of a metal by chemical reaction with substances in its environment, such as oxygen and water.
The corrosion of iron or steel in the presence of both oxygen and water, forming hydrated iron(III) oxide.
The chemical name for rust — a flaky, orange-brown compound formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

flashcard_questions.a: A corrosion-resistant bluish-white metal used to coat iron and steel in the galvanising process.
A method of rust prevention where a more reactive metal (such as zinc or magnesium) is placed in contact with iron, corroding preferentially to protect the iron.
